To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the rate of responding in the unchanged component increased when the schedule of reinforcement in the other component changed from variable-interval to extinction, and (2) the rate of local responding increased in the unchanged component when the schedule of the other component changed, and the rate of local interresponse time decreased in the unchanged component.

(a) the local rate of response at the beginning of a variable-interval component and immediately after a food reinforcer increased in the presence of an extinction component and (b) the interresponse time analysis revealed a similar increase in the relative frequency with which short interresponse times occurred at the beginning of and after food presentation.

increases in local response rate and interresponse-time measures at the beginning of an unchanged variable-interval component and immediately after reinforcement in a multiple variable-interval extinction schedule may be responsible for the increases in overall response rates in this schedule arrangement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of extinction of a component of a multiple schedule on response rates in the component in which reinforcement continues to be available.
the effect of the multiple variable interval 3 min extinction schedule on the behavior of the pigeons in the multiple variable interval variable interval 3-min schedule.
the analysis of behavioral contrast in terms of local rates of response and interresponse time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data were not consistent with a postreinforcement-pause explanation of the results.

behavioral contrast is an interaction between the local rate of response at the beginning of a component and the local rate of responding immediately after food presentation in the other component, with the relative frequency of shorter-duration interresponse times also contributing.
the local rate-of-response and inter-response-time analyses of the data did not provide a clear picture of the behavioral mechanisms underlying the contrast effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
behavioral contrast is produced by a local rate of response increase and that interresponse-time analysis provides no evidence of a change in the distribution of interresponse times in contrast.
the local-rate-of-response analysis provides a more sensitive measure of contrast effects than does the interresponse-time analysis.
contrast is not due to a postreinforcement increase in response rate, but is due to a postfood increase in response rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
local rates at the beginning and immediately after food in the unchanged component increased in the presence of a multiple variable-interval extinction schedule.
behavioral contrast is not simply the opposite of behavioral matching.
local rate of response and interresponse time analyses are complementary in their contributions to the understanding of behavioral contrast.
